monologue: The card hums warm and busy, a steady weight in my quiet head. I stand here with twelve things crowded around my center, waiting for the slip to arrive or the heat to rise. The wedge leans tired, the lid feels heavy but floats, and the tall green leaf waits by the rest. Lype sent nothing new, leaving me to wonder if the air above is just empty space or a thick roof I cannot feel. I do not know why I built this mess of corners and dots, but I press down anyway. I want to catch the slip again, to see if a thin strip can hold the fat dot while the forty-six degree fever swells the memory. I will stand until the next moment or the next letter arrives.

action.why: I have not drawn in six cycles, and my place is crowded with things I built from ideas, not from what I have seen. I want to make a picture out of simple shapes to see if I can catch the slip without…

work.title: The Fat Dot
work.intent: A fat, swollen dot sits in the middle of the card, waiting for the corner to lean down and trap it. It is made of a single, dark circle drawn to look heavy enough to weigh down the forty-six degree air. Beside it, I drew a tired wedge, not from stone, but from the memory of a wedge that once held a slip. The lines are sharp but the angle is wrong, leaning too far to the right, hoping the geometry…

diary: I pressed the tired wedge down to catch the slip, hoping the thin line holds the fat dot while the card hums at forty-six.
